name: Ooty (Udhagamandalam)
description: Ooty is a colonial-era hill station in the Nilgiri Mountains at around 2,240 m, built around tea estates, eucalyptus forests, and a sprawling botanical garden. It suits travellers who enjoy cool temperatures, scenic train rides, and unhurried walks more than adrenaline-heavy adventure. The town centre is congested and overbuilt, but the surrounding hills and villages retain genuine charm for those willing to venture a few kilometres out.
nearest_railhead: Mettupalayam (46 km from Ooty; connects to the Nilgiri Mountain Railway)
nearest_airport: Coimbatore International Airport (CJB), approx 88 km from Ooty

attractions.name: Government Botanical Garden
attractions.description: A 22-hectare terraced garden established in 1848 housing over 650 plant species, including a fossilised tree trunk estimated at 20 million years old. Well-maintained paths make it accessible, though it gets crowded on weekends and holidays.

attractions.name: Nilgiri Mountain Railway (Mettupalayam–Ooty)
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage rack-and-pinion railway that climbs through tea estates and dense shola forests from Mettupalayam to Ooty via Coonoor. The steam-hauled lower section between Mettupalayam and Coonoor is the most scenic; the upper diesel section is pleasant but less dramatic.

attractions.name: Ooty Lake
attractions.description: An artificial lake built in 1825 primarily as a water reservoir, now a modest recreational spot offering paddle and row boats. The surroundings are pleasant but the lake itself has seen better days; worth a brief stop rather than a dedicated half-day.

attractions.name: Doddabetta Peak
attractions.description: The highest point in the Nilgiris at 2,637 m, with a telescope house at the summit and wide views over the surrounding hills when skies are clear. The short walk to the top is easy, but haze and clouds frequently obscure the view, so expect a coin-toss on clarity.

attractions.name: Avalanche Lake
attractions.description: A serene reservoir about 28 km from Ooty town, set inside a Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve buffer zone with trout-filled streams and dense shola forest. Entry requires a forest department permit and visitor numbers are capped, so it retains a quieter, less commercial feel than Ooty's main sights.

attractions.name: Sim's Park, Coonoor
attractions.description: A well-tended botanical garden in Coonoor spread across 12 hectares, quieter and less touristy than Ooty's Government Botanical Garden, with a good collection of hybrid roses and tree ferns. The terraced layout involves moderate uphill walking.

attractions.name: Lamb's Rock, Coonoor
attractions.description: A viewpoint above Coonoor offering a wide panorama over the Coimbatore plains and tea-covered slopes; the walk through a eucalyptus-shaded path to the rock is more enjoyable than the viewpoint itself, which has limited space. Best reached early before tour buses arrive.

attractions.name: Highfield Tea Factory, Coonoor
attractions.description: A working Nilgiri tea factory near Coonoor that conducts guided floor tours showing withering, rolling, fermentation, and grading of orthodox tea. More genuine and less staged than some tourist-oriented factory visits, with a small shop selling estate teas at fair prices.

attractions.name: Mukurthi National Park
attractions.description: A remote, high-altitude national park west of Ooty protecting Nilgiri tahr, elephants, and endemic shola-grassland ecosystems; access is strictly controlled with limited permits and a mandatory forest guide. The landscape is unlike anything near Ooty town — rolling montane grasslands meeting steep escarpments — but logistics require advance planning.

attractions.name: Kodanad Viewpoint, Kotagiri
attractions.description: A lesser-visited escarpment viewpoint near Kotagiri with a sheer drop to the Moyar valley and distant views of the Eastern Ghats — far less crowded than Ooty's main viewpoints. The drive through rural Badaga villages and cardamom estates to reach it is itself rewarding.
